gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-nanum-myeongjo: Blunt and confident, Aaargh draws every line with a plain, unshaded stroke. Nanum Myeongjo, a refined text serif, tapers gently like a sharpened pencil line, so give it a modest size and let it breathe.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-noto-serif-hk: Noto Serif HK has a generous gap where each curve ends, with crossbars a touch thinner than its stems. And Aaargh holds its thickness steady around every bend, so a long passage moves from firm headline to a dignified, flowing text.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-noto-serif-jp: Solid and unfussy up top, Aaargh keeps the wall of every o constant. Noto Serif JP softens each curve with faint contrast.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-noto-serif-kr: Noto Serif KR reads with wide, barely curled s shapes. Beneath Aaargh's flat, unmodulated lines, its measured swell from hairline to stem gives a long stretch of text a smooth, classic pace.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-noto-serif-sc: Aaargh draws its letters with a thickness that never shifts with direction, giving a strong, commanding top line. But Noto Serif SC, a literary classic serif, supplies the finer bar widths, and that gap in texture is what makes the pair memorable.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-noto-serif-tc: Aaargh keeps an unvarying line thickness, with a generous opening into every e. And Noto Serif TC sits beneath it with slightly thinner connections at the stems, a traditional classic serif that holds its shapes open.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-petrona: Dignified is the word for Petrona, yet Aaargh gets the first say with horizontals as heavy as its verticals. Petrona then settles in with shallow curled terminals and a tempered contrast, like lightly engraved brass, so a long passage glides along.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-poly: Poly is bookish and literary, its bowls thinning slightly at the sides while terminals pull back from the curve. Poly's mild, approachable contrast sits under Aaargh's plain constant-width lines, a text serif following a display voice with no friction.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-quattrocento: Quattrocento lets daylight into every curve, its horizontal strokes slimmer than the verticals. But Aaargh's rounded-rod, single-weight build is the real hook, a stark difference in construction that keeps the pair lively.
gen-dafont-aaargh-gf-radley: Aaargh holds the steady line of a technical drafting pen, strong and commanding from the first word. Radley adds lightly shaded texture beneath it.
